$schema: one entry per logical Garmin Connect operation this project depends on. method+path from live probing or from decompiling the Garmin Connect Android client (v5.29, 2026-09). lastVerified is when the status below was actually observed. observedStatus is what came back, not what is hoped for.

auth.notes: CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-09-16. This answers design.md Open Question 1: a CAS service ticket IS exchangeable for a long-lived OAuth1 token, and with login-url=https://connect.garmin.com/modern -- NOT only garth's https://sso.garmin.com/sso/embed, which was the open worry when this entry was first added. Evidence: a real device completed sign-in and immediately performed authenticated reads (dailyFoodLog returned today's calories), which is impossible without a valid OAuth1 token stored by this route. Status recorded as 200 by inference from that success rather than from a logged response line; correct it if a real capture ever says otherwise. The three defects that made the earlier attempt fail were: login-url naming a different CAS service than the ticket was minted for, and an OAuth1 signature that both kept the query string on the base string URI and signed an empty oauth_token. Response parses as a query-string body carrying oauth_token/oauth_token_secret, as modelled on garth -- that shape is now confirmed too, since a wrong guess would have thrown malformedExchangeResponse instead of authenticating.

OAuth1-signed request, returns an OAuth2 access token valid ~24h (observed expires_in=88227s). This is the only working auth path since Garmin blocked scripted SSO login behind Cloudflare in March 2026 -- see garth's deprecation. Verified by live use in tools/lib/garmin-auth.mjs.

read.notes: Legacy/general daily summary. Exposes consumedKilocalories, remainingKilocalories, activeKilocalories, bmrKilocalories -- but consumedKilocalories was observed null even on a date where nutrition-service/food/logs/{date} showed real logged food. Do not treat this as the nutrition source of truth; it appears to be a separate, disconnected field. Kept only as a control route to confirm auth is alive. UPDATE 2026-09-23 (plan-testing-feedback, live probe via tools/garmin-get.mjs): 200, and the calorie fields are confirmed with real values mid-day: activeKilocalories 290, bmrKilocalories 920, totalKilocalories 1210, wellnessActiveKilocalories 290 (same as active), consumedKilocalories null, remainingKilocalories 3237. activeKilocalories is a running partial-day total for today. Planned use: the home screen's 'Active today' line (show-active-calories, in fix-testing-feedback-quick-wins). IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-23 (fix-testing-feedback-quick-wins): GarminClient.dailyUserSummary(date:) decodes only calendarDate/activeKilocalories/bmrKilocalories/totalKilocalories (DailyUserSummary). Re-probed read-only the same day for calendarDate=2026-09-22: 200, activeKilocalories 1031, bmrKilocalories 2252, totalKilocalories 3283 (plain JSON integers) -- a past day returns its full-day values. Any failure hides the line; never an error surface.

FatSecret- and Garmin-sourced results. Czech terms return results. Parameter name was discovered from a 400 error body naming 'searchFood.arg0.searchExpression'. Response: { results: [{ type, foodMetaData: { foodId, foodName, foodType, source (FATSECRET|GARMIN), regionCode, languageCode }, nutritionContents: [{ servingId, servingUnit, numberOfUnits, calories, carbs, protein, fat, fiber, sugar, saturatedFat, monounsaturatedFat, polyunsaturatedFat, cholesterol, sodium, potassium, vitaminA, vitaminC, calcium, iron, unitHasServing }], isFavorite, isRecent, servingQty, logTimestamp }], moreDataAvailable }. regionCode/languageCode are response-only, not accepted as query filters (tried, got 400). UPDATE 2026-09-23 (rebuild-food-search task 1.1/1.3, read-only probes via tools/garmin-get.mjs): PAGING -- the 400 for start=5 names the bound object: "'searchFood.arg0' Start index must be divisible by limit. (provided value: FoodSearchParams(searchExpression=rohlik, regionCode=US, languageCode=en, start=5, limit=20))", so start/limit/regionCode/languageCode are all real params, default limit is 20, default region US. start=20&limit=20 for "chicken" -> 200, 20 new results, moreDataAvailable true (and page start=40 too); limit=50 -> 50 results; limit=100 -> 400 "Maximum value for a fat secret search is 50"; limit=0 -> 400 (modulo by zero); start/limit=abc -> 404. moreDataAvailable is reliable: false when the term ran out ("rohlik" 13 results, start=20 -> 0 results, false), true when another page exists. pageNumber/pageSize are silently IGNORED (same 13 results). REGION -- regionCode=CZ is accepted and switches FatSecret to its Czech catalogue: "tvaroh" US-default -> 5 unrelated hits (Cheese [Dvaro], Carrot Sticks [Taro Brand]...), CZ -> 20+ real Czech tvarohy (Madeta, Tatra, Pilos, Albert...) with moreDataAvailable true and a working start=20 page; "kure" US -> "Pure [Organifi]" etc., CZ -> Kuřecí šunka/Kuře Pikant...; "mleko" US -> 0, CZ -> 20 (Mléko [Tatra] ...); "eidam" US 6 -> CZ 20+. English generics still come back under CZ ("chicken" -> Chicken, Chicken Breast; "banan" -> Banana; "smoked tofu" -> Smoked Tofu). Results carry foodMetaData.regionCode "CZ"/languageCode "en" -- the owner's own diary (food/logs/2026-09-22) already contains FATSECRET and GARMIN foods with regionCode CZ, so that tuple is loggable. regionCode=XX -> 400 "Region code is not supported"; languageCode=cs -> 400 "Language code is not supported". DIACRITICS (task 1.3) -- the search is diacritic-sensitive: "rohlik" 13 (all unrelated, e.g. Prepared Squid [Rolin]) vs "rohlík" 0; "banan" 20 vs "banán" 13 (different sets); CZ "bily jogurt" vs "bílý jogurt" return different Czech yogurts; "tvaroh odtucneny" missed Madeta's "Tvaroh Odtučněný" that "tvaroh odtučněný" found. DECISION: FoodLogCore.GarminSearchSource sends regionCode=CZ, limit=50, start=page*50, and both spellings (typed + diacritic-folded, or typed + diacritics restored from a small Czech food vocabulary), merged by foodId. Garmin also answers Czech words with loosely related English foods ("jogurt" -> Yogurt), and with garbage for unknown words; SearchRanker filters/ranks all of it client-side.
Confirmed param name via 400 body: 'getAutocompleteSuggestions.arg0' searchExpression query parameter must be provided -- same param name as foodSearch. Not yet tested with a real term.

Route confirmed to exist: no-param request returns 400 naming 'getFoodByBarCode.arg1' and 'barCode query parameter must be provided'. A real-looking EAN-13 (8594001020010) returned 404, which is 'no product for this barcode', not 'route missing' -- distinguishable because the no-param case was 400, not 404. Needs a barcode known to exist in the DB to confirm the success payload shape.

GET returned 404 (expected -- this is POST-shaped, per the write-request nature of an image upload). Not exercised as POST. Out of scope for this project's MVP -- app's own VisionKit barcode scan covers the barcode case, and barcode scanning itself was deprioritized 2026-09-14 (see garmin-food-log-contract.md) after the owner found Garmin's own native scanner doesn't recognize Czech barcodes. THE CORRECT read route -- plural 'logs', not 'log'. The vault's scripts/lib/garmin.mjs calls the singular '/nutrition-service/food/log/date/{date}', which 404s; that one-letter difference is why getNutritionLog() has silently returned null since it was written. Confirmed live with real data present on this account for 2026-09-14. Response top level: { mealDate, dayStartTime, dayEndTime, dailyViewType, dailyNutritionGoals: { calories, adjustedCalories, carbs, adjustedCarbs, fat, adjustedFat, protein, adjustedProtein }, dailyNutritionContent: { calories, carbs, fat, protein, caloriesPercentage }, mealDetails: [{ meal: { mealId, mealIndex, mealName (BREAKFAST/...), displayOrder, startTime, endTime, goals, editable, translated }, mealNutritionContent, mealNutritionGoals, loggedFoods: [{ id, logId, logTimestamp, logSource (GCM observed), logCategory (REGULAR_LOG observed), servingQty, foodMetaData, nutritionContent, isFavorite, mealId, customMealId, mealTime, foodInactive, type }] }], loggedFoodsWithServingSizes: [...] }. dayStartTime/dayEndTime were 04:00:00/17:00:00 on the observed day -- the nutrition 'day' window is configurable and is NOT simple local midnight-to-midnight; account for this when reading 'today'.

Shape inspected 2026-09-16: { meals: [{ mealId (number, a per-date meal INSTANCE id), mealName (BREAKFAST|LUNCH|DINNER|SNACKS), startTime, endTime }], dailyTimelineStartTime, dailyTimelineEndTime, dailyViewType }. BREAKFAST/LUNCH/DINNER carry an HH:mm:ss window; SNACKS carries none. Returned whether or not anything is logged. This is where createFoodLogEntry gets its mealId, which is why GarminClient.createFoodLogEntry calls it first.

Sibling paths, still only decompiled-string-literal tier (Android client v5.29, unverified further this pass): POST /nutrition-service/favorite/food, DELETE /nutrition-service/favorite/food/{foodId}, GET/POST /nutrition-service/favorite/meal -- worth a live device probe (POST with an empty or minimal body against a known foodId) before ever trying to close this out, since the 405 rules out GET but says nothing about what POST needs.

Shape: { weightChangeType (LOSS observed), targetDate, weightChangeRate, activeDailyCalories, userDefinedActiveCalories, calorieGoal, macroGoals: { carbs, fat, protein }, autoCalorieAdjustment, regionCode, languageCode, dailyTimelineStartTime, dailyTimelineEndTime, startingWeight, targetWeightGoal, effectiveDate, nutritionStatus (ACTIVE observed) }. macroGoals are GRAMS: they equalled the daily log's base (non-adjusted) goals exactly on the probed day. Read-only in this app (GarminClient.nutritionSettings); garmin_mcp writes it with PUT to the same path, which this project does not use. UPDATE 2026-09-22 (fix-custom-food-log-region): regionCode/languageCode were part of this confirmed shape from the start but never decoded into the Swift model until now -- a real device 400 logging a just-created custom food ('Custom food nutrition information is missing for the provided food id with region code and language code') traced back to every food-log/custom-food write always hardcoding regionCode='US'/languageCode='en' regardless of the account's real values here. Both are now decoded and threaded through as an optional override on food-log writes and custom-food creation, falling back to the old hardcoded constants when unavailable. Still unconfirmed which actual value this account's regionCode/languageCode carries -- that requires a real device read, not assumed here. UPDATE 2026-09-23: live read shows the weight-goal fields populated -- weightChangeType LOSS, weightChangeRate 250, startingWeight 80400, targetWeightGoal 76000, calorieGoal 2300. Weights are GRAMS (80400 = 80.4 kg, matching the weight-service's own gram units); weightChangeRate 250 is presumed grams/week. Planned use: the weight goal card (sync-weight-hydration-with-garmin).

Confirmed live via probe-garmin-nutrition.mjs. Candidate for a cheaper 'just the running total' read than the full dailyFoodLog payload -- worth inspecting its response shape before defaulting every widget refresh to the heavier route.

Confirmed live with a real date range. Accepts a MULTI-DAY range in one call -- more efficient than calling dailyFoodLog once per day for a trend view. Response: { startDate, endDate, caloriesBurned, mealNutritionContents: [], dailyNutritionContents: [{ mealDate, nutritionContent?: { calories, carbs, fat, protein, otherCalories, caloriesPercentage }, nutritionGoals?: { calories, adjustedCalories, carbs, adjustedCarbs, fat, adjustedFat, protein, adjustedProtein } }], averageNutritionContents: {} }. Days with no logged food omit nutritionContent/nutritionGoals entirely (bare { mealDate }) rather than returning zeros -- treat a missing key as 'nothing logged', not an error. nutritionGoals values cross-checked exactly against dailyFoodLog's dailyNutritionGoals for the same day (2300/3128/316/430/64/87/115/156) -- consistent between routes. Sibling: /nutrition-service/calorie/summary/weekly, same param shape presumed, not tested. UPDATE 2026-09-22 (add-trends-and-insights): now actually implemented and called -- GarminClient.calorieSummaryDaily, decoded via CalorieSummaryDailyResponse/CalorieSummaryDay in GarminModels.swift, reusing DailyNutritionContent/NutritionGoals -- and used by the Trends screen's ~30-day macro chart (MacroTrendLoader). The profile the Garmin Connect app shows: displayName, fullName, userName, location, profileImageUrlSmall/Medium/Large, plus many visibility flags and Garmin's own userLevel/userPoint (unrelated to this app's XP and deliberately not shown). GarminClient.socialProfile decodes only the name, location and photo fields. Same route python-garminconnect uses for get_full_name. UPDATE 2026-09-23: on this account displayName is a UUID ('f8c8e6e5-...'), NOT a human name -- which is exactly what the Profile header was showing, because it preferred displayName over fullName. fullName carries the real 'first last' name. profileId is also present (numeric). write.notes: CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-09-16: a real device logged a FATSECRET food to DINNER and it read back once, filed under the right meal, with logSource GCW, logCategory REGULAR_LOG, mealTime equal to the meal window start, servingQty as sent, and regionCode US. write.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-22; evidence tier corrected AGAIN the same day after a second verification pass -- read that second correction below before trusting the first. Real device attempt (2026-09-21) returned 400 BadRequestException: 'custom food nutrition information is missing for the provided food id with region code and language code' against the original flat, decompiled-string-literal-tier POST guess. A first attempted fix (adding top-level regionCode/languageCode) did NOT resolve it -- the user reported the identical error again on a later real-device attempt. Root cause: the envelope shape itself was wrong, not a missing field. Corrected contract, ported from tamcore/garmin-mcp (github.com/tamcore/garmin-mcp), internal/garmin/api/nutritionwritefood.go (fetched 2026-09-22 in full): method is PUT, not POST; body is { foodMetaData: { foodId (omitted on create), foodName, foodType: 'GENERIC', source: 'GARMIN', regionCode, languageCode, brandName (omitted if none) }, nutritionContents: [ { servingId (omitted on create), servingUnit, numberOfUnits, calories, carbs, protein, fat, ...every macro/micro optional } ] } -- nutritionContents is a ONE-ELEMENT ARRAY, a sibling of foodMetaData, not nested inside it. Every numeric field inside nutritionContents is a STRING ('160', never 160), dropping a trailing '.0' for a whole number. EVIDENCE TIER, corrected on a second pass the same day: this was first claimed as 'the same evidence tier as addWeighIn/addHydration' (a real, verifiable upstream file citation) -- that claim was WRONG and has been checked and disproven, not just walked back on suspicion. tamcore/garmin-mcp's own doc comments cite 'cyberjunky/python-garminconnect, nutrition.py:360-363' as the source, but that repository has NO nutrition.py file and NO custom-food code at all, checked directly by cloning both the exact pinned commit tamcore's own THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md cites (414b540, release 0.3.10) and the current main branch and grepping both -- zero matches for 'custom' anywhere. The citation is fabricated or mislabeled, not real. What DOES hold up, also checked directly: tamcore/garmin-mcp has a real, build-tag-gated live-account integration test (live/nutritionwrite_test.go, '//go:build garminlive') that creates/updates/logs/deletes a custom food against an actual Garmin account and asserts on the real response fields, and its tool handler is traced to call the exact same buildCustomFoodBody function whose structs were ported here -- real, structured, apparently-live-tested code, meaningfully better than a blind guess, but NOT independently verified from this project's own vantage point (no way to confirm that live test has actually been run and passed recently) and its own internal citations cannot be trusted at face value going forward. Response is decoded as the existing FoodSearchResult type (an educated guess, not confirmed). Not yet retried against the real account since either correction -- see GarminModels.swift's CustomFoodWriteBody doc comment for the full reasoning, still gated behind the same explicit user-triggered 'Create in Garmin' action.

add-weight-tracking. Source: cyberjunky/python-garminconnect (github.com/cyberjunky/python-garminconnect), garminconnect/__init__.py's add_weigh_in/add_weigh_in_with_timestamps (~lines 1414-1483) and the shared _fmt_ts helper (~line 221), fetched 2026-09-22 -- a real, actively-maintained, widely-used OSS client's actual request shape, not a decompiled string literal or blind guess: { dateTimestamp, gmtTimestamp, unitKey ('kg'|'lbs'), sourceType: 'MANUAL', value }, both timestamps formatted yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS (naive/no offset), dateTimestamp in local time and gmtTimestamp the same instant in UTC. This app always sends unitKey='kg' (no imperial/metric setting exists anywhere in GarminFood). Never yet called by this project against the real account -- gated the same way createFoodLogEntry is (delivery only via WeightOutbox's durable queue, never a synchronous UI call), NOT gated behind an extra confirmation dialog the way createCustomFood/createCustomMeal are, since logging a weight IS the deliberate user action, same status as a food log entry. UPDATE 2026-09-23: CONFIRMED. The owner reported device weigh-ins arriving in Garmin, and a live probe (tools/garmin-write-probe.mjs, owner-approved) POSTed {dateTimestamp '2026-09-23T03:03:03.000', gmtTimestamp '2026-09-23T01:03:03.000', unitKey 'kg', sourceType 'MANUAL', value 83.9} -> 204 No Content (empty body), and the sample appeared in weighInsDayView (samplePk 1790152598056). It was then deleted via weighInDelete.
